18.16: According to al that thou desiredst of the Lord thy God in Horeb, in the day of the assemblie, when thou saidest, Let me hear the voice of my Lord God no more, nor see this great fire any more, that I die not.
18.17: And the Lord sayde unto me, They have well spoken.
18.18: I will raise them up a Prophet from among their brethren like unto thee, and will put my woordes in his mouth, and he shall speak unto them all that I shall commaund him.
18.19: And whosoever will not hearken unto my wordes, which he shall speak in my Name, I will require it of him.
18.20: But the prophet that shall presume to speak a word in my name, which I have not commanded him to speak, or that speaketh in the name of other gods, even the same prophet shall die.
18.21: And if thou think in thine heart, How shall we know the word which the Lord hath not spoken?
18.22: When a prophet speaketh in the Name of the Lord, if the thing follow not nor come to pass, that is the thing which the Lord hath not spoken, but the prophet hath spoken it presumptuously: thou shalt not therefore be afraid of him.

19.1: When the Lord thy God shall root out the nations, whose land the Lord thy God giveth thee, and thou shalt possess them, and dwell in their cities, and in their houses,
19.2: Thou shalt separate three cities for thee in the middes of thy land which the Lord thy God giveth thee to possess it.
19.3: Thou shalt prepare thee the way, and deuide the coastes of the land, which the Lord thy God giveth thee to inherit, into three parts, that every manslayer may flee thither.
19.4: This also is ye cause wherfore the manslayer shall flee thither, and live: who so killeth his neighbor ignorantly, and hated him not in time passed:
19.5: As hee that goeth unto the wood with his neighbor to hew wood, and his hand striketh with the axe to cut down the tree, if the head slip from the helve, and hit his neighbour that he dieth, the same shall flee unto one of the cities, and live,
19.6: Least the avenger of the blood follow after the manslayer, while his heart is chafed, and overtake him, because the way is long, and slaie him, although he be not worthy of death, because he hated him not in time passed.
19.7: Wherefore I command thee, saying, Thou shalt appoint out three cities for thee.
19.8: And when the Lord thy God enlargeth thy coastes (as he hath sworn unto thy fathers) and giveth thee all the land which he promised to give unto thy fathers,
19.9: (If thou keep all these commandements to doe them, which I commaund thee this day: to wit, that thou love the Lord thy God, and walk in his waies for ever) then shalt thou add three cities moe for thee besides those three,
19.10: That innocent bloude be not shed within thy land, which the Lord thy God giveth thee to inherit, lest bloud be upon thee.
19.11: But if a man hate his neighbour, and lay wait for him, and rise against him, and smite any man that he die, and flee unto any of these cities,
19.12: Then the Elders of his citie shall send and set him thence, and deliver him into the hands of the avenger of the blood, that he may die.
19.13: Thine eye shall not spare him, but thou shalt put away the crie of innocent blood from Israel, that it may goe well with thee.
19.14: Thou shalt not remooue thy neighbours mark, which they of old time have set in thine inheritance, that thou shalt inherit in the land, which ye Lord thy God giveth thee to possess it.
19.15: One witnes shall not rise against a man for any trespass, or for any sinne, or for any fault that hee offendeth in, but at the mouth of two witnesses or at the mouth of three witnesses shall the matter be stablished.
19.16: If a false witness rise up against a man to accuse him of trespass,
19.17: Then both the men which strive together, shall stand before ye Lord, even before the Priests and the Judges, which shall be in those daies,
19.18: And the Judges shall make diligent inquisition: and if the witness be found false, and hath given false witnes against his brother,
19.19: Then shall yee doe unto him as hee had thought to doe unto his brother: so thou shalt take evil away forth of the middes of thee.
19.20: And the rest shall hear this, and fear, and shall henceforth commit no more any such wickednes among you.
19.21: Therefore thine eye shall have no compassion, but life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.

20.1: When thou shalt go forth to war against thine enemies, and shalt see horses and charets, and people moe then thou, be not afrayde of them: for the Lord thy God is with thee, which brought thee out of the land of Egypt.
20.2: And when ye are come neere unto the battel, then the Priest shall come forth to speak unto the people,
20.3: And shall say unto them, Hear, O Israel: ye are come this day unto battell against your enemies: let not your heartes faynt, neither fear, nor be amased, nor adread of them.
20.4: For ye Lord your God goeth with you, to fight for you against your enemies, and to save you
20.5: And let the officers speak unto the people, saying, What man is there that hath buylt a new house, and hath not dedicate it? let him go and return to his house, least he dye in the battel, and an other man dedicate it.
20.6: And what man is there that hath planted a vineyard, and hath not eaten of the fruit? let him go and return again unto his house, least he die in the battel, and another eat the fruit.
20.7: And what man is there that hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her? let him go and return again unto his house, lest he die in the battell, and another man take her.
20.8: And let the officers speak further unto the people, and say, Whosoever is afrayde and faynt hearted, let him go and return unto his house, least his brethrens heart faynt like his heart.
20.9: And after that the officers have made an end of speaking unto the people, they shall make captaines of the armie to govern the people.
20.10: When thou comest neere unto a citie to fight against it, thou shalt offer it peace.
20.11: And if it answer thee again peaceably, and open unto thee, then let all the people that is found therein, be tributaries unto thee, and serve thee.
20.12: But if it will make no peace with thee, but make war against thee, then shalt thou besiege it.
20.13: And the Lord thy God shall deliver it into thine handes, and thou shalt smite all the males thereof with the edge of the sword.
20.14: Onely the women, and the children, and the cattel, and all that is in the citie, even all the spoyle thereof shalt thou take unto thy self, and shalt eat the spoyle of thine enemies, which the Lord thy God hath given thee.
20.15: Thus shalt thou do unto all ye cities, which are a great way off from thee, which are not of the cities of these nations here.
20.16: But of the cities of this people, which the Lord thy God shall give thee to inherit, thou shalt save no person alive,
20.17: But shalt utterly destroy them: to wit, the Hittites, and the Amorites, the Canaanites, and the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, as the Lord thy God hath commanded thee,
20.18: That they teach you not to doe after all their abominations, which they have done unto their gods, and so ye should sinne against the Lord your God.
20.19: When thou hast besieged a citie long time, and made war against it to take it, destroy not the trees therof, by smiting an axe into them: for thou mayest eat of them: therfore thou shalt not cut them down to further thee in the siege, (for the tree of the field is mans life)
20.20: Onely those trees, which thou knowest are not for meat, those shalt thou destroy and cut down, and make fortes against the citie that maketh war with thee, until thou subdue it.

21.1: If one be found slain in the land, which the Lord thy God giveth thee to possess it, lying in the field, and it is not know who hath slain him,
21.2: Then thine Elders and thy Judges shall come forth, and measure unto the cities that are round about him that is slayne.
21.3: Aud let ye Elders of that citie, which is next unto the slain man, take out of the drove an heifer that hath not been put to labour, nor hath drawen in the yoke.
21.4: And let the Elders of that citie bring the heifer unto a stonie valley, which is neyther eared nor sowen, and strike off the heifers neck there in the valley.
21.5: Also the Priests the sonnes of Levi (whom the Lord thy God hath chosen to minister, and to bless in the name of the Lord) shall come forth, and by their word shall all strife and plague be tried.
21.6: And all the Elders of that citie that came neere to the slayne man, shall wash their hands over the heifer that is beheaded in the valley:
21.7: And shall testifie, and say, Our handes have not shed this blood, neither have our eies seen it.
21.8: O Lord, be merciful unto thy people Israel, whom thou hast redeemed, and lay no innocent blood to the charge of thy people Israel, and the blood shalbe forgiven them.
21.9: So shalt thou take away the cry of innocet blood from thee, when thou shalt do that which is right in the sight of the Lord.
21.10: Whe thou shalt go to war against thine enemies, and the Lord thy God shall deliver them into thine hands, and thou shalt take the captives,
21.11: And shalt see among the captives a beautiful woman, and hast a desire unto her, and wouldest take her to thy wife,
21.12: Then thou shalt bring her home to thine house, and she shall shave her head, and pare her nayles,
21.13: And she shall put off the garment that she was taken in, and she shall remain in thine house, and bewail her father and her mother a moneth long: and after that shalt thou go in unto her, and marry her, and she shalbe thy wife.
21.14: And if thou have no fauour unto her, then thou mayest let her go whither she will, but thou shalt not sell her for money, nor make marchandise of her, because thou hast humbled her.
21.15: If a man have two wives, one loved and another hated, and they have borne him children, both the loved and also the hated: if the first borne be the sonne of the hated,
21.16: Then when the time cometh, that hee appointeth his sonnes to be heires of that which he hath, he may not make the sonne of the beloved first borne before the sonne of the hated, which is the first borne:
21.17: But he shall acknowledge the sonne of the hated for the first borne, and give him double portion of all that he hath: for hee is the first of his strength, and to him belongeth the right of the first borne.
21.18: If any man have a sonne that is stubburne and disobedient, which wil not hearken unto the voice of his father, nor the voyce of his mother, and they have chastened him, and he would not obey them,
21.19: Then shall his father and his mother take him, and bring him out unto the Elders of his citie, and unto the gate of the place where he dwelleth,
21.20: And shall say unto the Elders of his citie, This our sonne is stubburne and disobedient, and he wil not obey our admonition: he is a riotour, and a drunkard.
21.21: Then all the men of his citie shall stone him with stones unto death: so thou shalt take away evil from among you, that all Israel may hear it, and fear.
21.22: If a man also have committed a trespass worthy of death, and is put to death, and thou hangest him on a tree,
21.23: His body shall not remain all night upon the tree, but thou shalt bury him the same day: for the curse of God is on him that is hanged. Defile not therfore thy land which the Lord thy God giveth thee to inherit.

22.1: Thou shalt not see thy brothers oxe nor his sheep go astray, and withdraw thy self from them, but shalt bring the again unto thy brother.
22.2: And if thy brother bee not neere unto thee, or if thou know him not, then thou shalt bring it into thine house, and it shall remain with thee, until thy brother seek after it: then shalt thou deliver it to him again.
22.3: In like maner shalt thou do with his ass, and so shalt thou do with his rayment, and shalt so doe with all lost things of thy brother, which he hath lost: if thou hast found them, thou shalt not withdraw thy self from them.
22.4: Thou shalt not see thy brothers ass nor his oxe fal down by the way, and withdraw thy self from them, but shalt lift them up with him.
22.5: The woman shall not wear that which perteineth unto the man, neither shall a man put on womans rayment: for all that doe so, are abomination unto the Lord thy God.
22.6: If thou find a birdes nest in the way, in any tree, or on the ground, whether they be yong or egges, and the damme sitting upon the yong, or upon the egges, thou shalt not take ye damme with the yong,
22.7: But shalt in any wise let the damme go, and take the yong to thee, that thou mayest prosper and prolong thy dayes.
22.8: When thou buildest a new house, thou shalt make a battlemet on thy roof, that thou lay not blood upon thine house, if any man fal thence.
22.9: Thou shalt not sow thy vineyard with divers kinds of seedes, lest thou defile the increase of the seed which thou hast sowen, and the fruit of the vineyard.
22.10: Thou shalt not plow with an oxe and an ass together.
22.11: Thou shalt not wear a garment of divers sorts, as of woollen and linen together.
22.12: Thou shalt make thee fringes upon the four quarters of thy vesture, wherewith thou coverest thy self.
22.13: If a man take a wife, and when he hath lyen with her, hate her,
22.14: And lay slaunderous thinges unto her charge, and bring up an evil name upon her, and say, I took this wife, and when I came to her, I found her not a mayde,
22.15: Then shall the father of the mayde and her mother take and bring the signes of the maydes virginitie unto the Elders of the citie to the gate.
22.16: And the maydes father shall say unto the Elders, I gave my daughter unto this man to wife, and he hateth her:
22.17: And lo, he layeth slaunderous things unto her charge, saying, I found not thy daughter a mayde: loe, these are the tokens of my daughters virginitie: and they shall spread the vesture before the Elders of the citie.
22.18: Then the Elders of the citie shall take that man and chastise him,
22.19: And shall condemn him in an hundreth shekels of silver, and give them unto the father of the mayde, because he hath brought up an evil name upon a mayde of Israel: and she shalbe his wife, and he may not put her away all his life.
22.20: But if this thing be true, that the mayde be not found a virgin,
22.21: Then shall they bring forth the mayde to the door of her fathers house, and the men of her citie shall stone her with stones to death: for she hath wrought follie in Israel, by playing ye whore in her fathers house: so thou shalt put evil away from among you.
22.22: If a man be found lying with a woman marryed to a man, then they shall dye even both twain: to wit, the man that lay with the wife, and the wife: so thou shalt put away evil from Israel.
22.23: If a maid be betrothed unto an husband, and a man find her in the town and lye with her,
22.24: Then shall yee bring them both out unto the gates of the same citie, and shall stone them with stones to death: the mayde because she cried not, being in the citie, and the man, because he hath humbled his neighbours wife: so thou shalt put away evil from among you.
22.25: But if a man find a betrothed mayde in the field, and force her, and lye with her, then the man that lay with her, shall dye alone:
22.26: And unto the mayd thou shalt do nothing, because there is in the mayde no cause of death: for as when a man riseth against his neighbour and woundeth him to death, so is this matter.
22.27: For he found her in the fieldes: the betrothed mayde cryed, and there was no man to succour her.
22.28: If a man find a mayde that is not betrothed, and take her, and lye with her, and they be found,
22.29: Then the man that lay with her, shall give unto the maydes father fiftie shekels of silver: and she shalbe his wife, because he hath humbled her: he can not put her away all his life.
22.30: No man shall take his fathers wife, nor shall vncouer his fathers skirt.

23.1: None that is hurt by bursting, or that hath his priuie member cut off, shall enter into the Congregation of the Lord.
23.2: A bastard shall not enter into the Congregation of the Lord: even to his tenth generation shall he not enter into the Congregation of the Lord.
23.3: The Ammonites and the Moabites shall not enter into the Congregation of the Lord: even to their tenth generation shall they not enter into the Congregation of the Lord for ever,
23.4: Because they met you not with bread and water in the way, when yee came out of Egypt, and because they hyred against thee Balaam the sonne of Beor, of Pethor in Aram-naharaim, to curse thee.
23.5: Nevertheless, the Lord thy God would not hearken unto Balaam, but the Lord thy God turned the curse to a blessing unto thee, because the Lord thy God loved thee.
23.6: Thou shalt not seek their peace nor their prosperitie all thy dayes for ever.
23.7: Thou shalt not abhorre an Edomite: for he is thy brother, neither shalt thou abhorre an Egyptian, because thou wast a strager in his land.
23.8: The children that are begotten of them in their third generation, shall enter into the Congregation of the Lord.
23.9: When thou goest out with the host against thine enemies, keep thee then from all wickedness.
23.10: If there be among you any that is vncleane by that which cometh to him by night, he shall goe out of the host, and shall not enter into the host,
23.11: But at even he shall wash him self with water, and when the sunne is down, he shall enter into the host.
23.12: Thou shalt have a place also without the host whither thou shalt resort,
23.13: And thou shalt have a paddle among thy weapons, and when thou wouldest sit down without, thou shalt shalt digge therewith, and returning thou shalt cover thine excrements.
23.14: For the Lord thy God walketh in the mids of thy camp to deliver thee, and to give thee thine enemies before thee: therefore thine host shalbe holy, that he see no filthie thing in thee and turn away from thee.
23.15: Thou shalt not deliver the servant unto his master, which is escaped from his master unto thee.
23.16: He shall dwell with thee, even among you, in what place he shall chuse, in one of thy cities where it liketh him best: thou shalt not vex him.
23.17: There shalbe no whore of the daughters of Israel, neither shall there be a whore keeper of the sonnes of Israel.
23.18: Thou shalt neyther bring the hyre of a whore, nor the price of a dogge into the house of the Lord thy God for any vow: for even both these are abomination unto the Lord thy God.
23.19: Thou shalt not give to vsurie to thy brother: as vsurie of money, vsurie of meat, vsurie of any thing that is put to vsurie.
23.20: Unto a stranger thou mayest lend upon vsurie, but thou shalt not lend upon vsurie unto thy brother, that the Lord thy God may bless thee in all that thou settest thine hand to, in the land whither thou goest to possess it.
23.21: When thou shalt vow a vow unto the Lord thy God, thou shalt not be slack to pay it: for the Lord thy God will surely require it of thee, and so it should be sinne unto thee.
23.22: But when thou absteinest from vowing, it shalbe no sinne unto thee.
23.23: That which is gone out of thy lippes, thou shalt keep and perform, as thou hast vowed it willingly unto the Lord thy God: for thou hast spoken it with thy mouth.
23.24: When thou comest unto thy neighbours vineyard, then thou mayest eat grapes at thy pleasure, as much as thou wilt: but thou shalt put none in thy vessell.
23.25: When thou comest into thy neighbours corn thou mayest pluck the eares with thine hand, but thou shalt not move a sickle to thy neighbours corn.

24.1: When a man taketh a wife, and marrieth her, if so be she find no fauour in his eyes, because hee hath espyed some filthiness in her, then let him write her a bill of divorcement, and put it in her hand, and send her out of his house.
24.2: And when she is departed out of his house, and gone her way, and marrie with an other man,
24.3: And if the latter husband hate her, and write her a letter of divorcement, and put it in her hand, and send her out of his house, or if the latter man die which took her to wife:
24.4: Then her first husband, which sent her away, may not take her again to be his wife, after that she is defiled: for that is abomination in the sight of the Lord, and thou shalt not cause the land to sinne, which the Lord thy God doeth give thee to inherit.
24.5: When a man taketh a new wife, he shall not goe a warfare, neither shalbe charged with any business, but shalbe free at home one yeere, and reioyce with his wife which he hath taken.
24.6: No man shall take the nether nor the upper milstone to pledge: for this gage is his living.
24.7: If any man be found stealing any of his brethren of the children of Israel, and maketh marchandise of him, or selleth him, that thief shall die: so shalt thou put evil away from among you.
24.8: Take heed of the plague of leprosie, that thou observe diligently, and doe according to all that the Priestes of the Levites shall teach you: take heed ye doe as I commanded them.
24.9: Remember what the Lord thy God did unto Miriam by the way after that ye were come out of Egypt.
24.10: Whe thou shalt ask again of thy neighbour any thing lent, thou shalt not goe into his house to fet his pledge.
24.11: But thou shalt stand without, and the man that borowed it of thee, shall bring the pledge out of the doores unto thee.
24.12: Furthermore if it be a poor body, thou shalt not sleep with his pledge,
24.13: But shalt restore him the pledge when the sunne goeth down, that he may sleep in his raiment, and bless thee: and it shalbe righteousness unto thee before the Lord thy God.
24.14: Thou shalt not oppress an hyred servant that is needie and poor, neyther of thy brethren, nor of the stranger that is in thy land within thy gates.
24.15: Thou shalt give him his hire for his day, neither shall the sunne goe down upon it: for he is poor, and therewith susteineth his life: lest he cry against thee unto the Lord, and it be sinne unto thee.
24.16: The fathers shall not be put to death for the children, nor the children put to death for the fathers, but every man shalbe put to death for his own sinne.
24.17: Thou shalt not pervert the right of the stranger, nor of the fatherless, nor take a widowes rayment to pledge.
24.18: But remember that thou wast a servant in Egypt, and how the Lord thy God delivered thee thence. Therefore I commaund thee to doe this thing.
24.19: When thou cuttest down thine harvest in thy field, and hast forgotten a sheaf in the field, thou shalt not goe again to fet it, but it shalbe for the stranger, for the fatherles, and for the widow: that the Lord thy God may bless thee in all the workes of thine hands.
24.20: When thou beatest thine olive tree, thou shalt not goe over the boughes again, but it shalbe for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow.
24.21: When thou gatherest thy vineyard, thou shalt not gather the grapes clean after thee, but they shalbe for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow.
24.22: And remember that thou wast a servant in the land of Egypt: therefore I command thee to doe this thing.

25.1: When there shall be strife between men, and they shall come unto iudgement, and sentence shall be given upon them, and the righteous shall be justified, and the wicked condemned,
25.2: Then if so be the wicked be worthy to bee beaten, the judge shall cause him to lie down, and to be beaten before his face, according to his trespass, unto a certain nomber.
25.3: Fortie stripes shall he cause him to have and not past, lest if he should exceed and beat him above that with many stripes, thy brother should appear despised in thy sight.
25.4: Thou shalt not mousell the oxe that treadeth out the corn.
25.5: If brethren dwell together, and one of them dye and have no sonne, the wife of the dead shall not marry without: that is, unto a stranger, but his kinseman shall goe in unto her, and take her to wife, and doe the kinsemans office to her.
25.6: And the first borne which she beareth, shall succeed in the name of his brother which is dead, that his name be not put out of Israel.
25.7: And if the man will not take his kinsewoman, then let his kinsewoman goe up to the gate unto the Elders, and say, My kinsman refuseth to rayse up unto his brother a name in Israel: hee will not doe the office of a kinsman unto me.
25.8: Then the Elders of his citie shall call him, and commune with him: if he stand and say, I wil not take her,
25.9: Then shall his kinswoman come unto him in the presence of the Elders, and loose his shooe from his foot, and spit in his face, and answer, and say, So shall it be done unto that man, that will not buylde up his brothers house.
25.10: And his name shall be called in Israel, The house of him whose shooe is put off.
25.11: When men strive together, one with another, if the wife of the one come neere, for to rid her husband out of the handes of him that smiteth him, and put foorth her hand, and take him by his priuities,
25.12: Then thou shalt cut off her hand: thine eye shall not spare her.
25.13: Thou shalt not have in thy bagge two maner of weightes, a great and a small,
25.14: Neither shalt thou have in thine house divers measures, a great and a small:
25.15: But thou shalt have a right and just weight: a perfite and a just measure shalt thou have, that thy dayes may be lengthened in the land, which the Lord thy God giveth thee.
25.16: For all that doe such things, and all that doe unrighteously, are abomination unto the Lord thy God.
25.17: Remember what Amalek did unto thee by the way, when ye were come out of Egypt:
25.18: How he met thee by ye way, and smote ye hindmost of you, all that were feeble behind thee, when thou wast fainted and weary, and he feared not God.
25.19: Therefore, when the Lord thy God hath given thee rest from all thine enemies round about in the land, which the Lord thy God giveth thee for an inheritance to possess it, then thou shalt put out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven: forget not.

26.1: Also when thou shalt come into the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee for inheritance, and shalt possess it, and dwell therein,
26.2: Then shalt thou take of the first of all the fruit of the earth, and bring it out of the land that the Lord thy God giveth thee, and put it in a basket, and goe unto the place, which the Lord thy God shall chose to place his Name there.
26.3: And thou shalt come unto the Priest, that shall be in those dayes, and say unto him, I acknowledge this day unto the Lord thy God, that I am come unto the countrey which the Lord sware unto our fathers for to give us.
26.4: Then the Priest shall take the basket out of thine hand, and set it down before the altar of the Lord thy God.
26.5: And thou shalt answer and say before the Lord thy God, A Syrian was my father, who being ready to perish for hunger, went down into Egypt, and soiourned there with a small company, and grew there unto a nation great, mightie and full of people.
26.6: And the Egyptians vexed us, and troubled us, and laded us with cruel bondage.
26.7: But when we cried unto the Lord God of our fathers, the Lord heard our voyce, and looked on our aduersitie, and on our labour, and on our oppression.
26.8: And the Lord brought us out of Egypt in a mightie hand, and a stretched out arm, with great terribleness, both in signes and wonders.
26.9: And he hath brought us into this place, and hath given us this land, even a land that floweth with milk and hony.
26.10: And now, lo, I have brought ye first fruites of the land which thou, O Lord, hast given me, and thou shalt set it before the Lord thy God, and worship before the Lord thy God:
26.11: And thou shalt reioyce in all the good things which the Lord thy God hath given unto thee and to thine houshold, thou and the Levite, and the stranger that is among you.
26.12: When thou hast made an end of tithing all the tythes of thine increase, the third yeere, which is the yeere of tithing, and hast given it unto the Levite, to the stranger, to the fatherless, and to the widow, that they may eat within thy gates, and be satisfied,
26.13: Then thou shalt say before the Lord thy God, I have brought the halowed thing out of mine house, and also have given it unto the Levites and to the strangers, to the fatherless, and to the widow, according to all thy comandements which thou hast commanded me: I have transgressed none of thy comandements, nor forgotten them.
26.14: I have not eaten therof in my mourning, nor suffred ought to perish through vncleannes, nor given ought thereof for the dead, but have hearkened unto the voyce of the Lord my God: I have done after al that thou hast comaded me.
26.15: Look down from thine holy habitation, even from heaven, and bless thy people Israel, and the land which thou hast given us (as thou swarest unto our fathers) the land that floweth with milk and hony.
26.16: This day the Lord thy God doeth command thee to do these ordinances, and lawes: keep them therefore, and do them with al thine heart, and with all thy soul.
26.17: Thou hast set up the Lord this day to be thy God, and to walk in his wayes, and to keep his ordinances, and his commandements, and his lawes, and to hearken unto his voyce.
26.18: And the Lord hath set thee up this day, to be a precious people unto him (as hee hath promised thee) and that thou shouldest keep all his commandements,
26.19: And to make thee high above al nations (which he hath made) in praise, and in name, and in glory, and that thou shouldest be an holy people unto the Lord thy God, as he hath said.

27.1: Then Moses with the Elders of Israel commanded the people, saying, Keep all the comandements, which I command you this day.
27.2: And when ye shall pass over Iorden unto the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee, thou shalt set thee up great stones, and playster them with plaister,
27.3: And shalt write upon them all the words of this Law, when thou shalt come over, that thou mayest go into the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee: a land that floweth with milk and hony, as the Lord God of thy fathers hath promised thee.
27.4: Therefore when ye shall pass over Iorden, ye shall set up these stones, which I command you this day in mount Ebal, and thou shalt plaister them with plaister.
27.5: And there shalt thou build unto the Lord thy God an altar, even an altar of stones: thou shalt lift none yron instrument upon them.
27.6: Thou shalt make the altar of the Lord thy God of whole stones, and offer burnt offerings thereon unto the Lord thy God.
27.7: And thou shalt offer peace offrings, and shalt eat there and reioyce before the Lord thy God:
27.8: And thou shalt write upon the stones al the words of this Law, well and plainely.
27.9: And Moses and the Priestes of the Levites spake unto all Israel, saying, Take heed and hear, O Israel: this day thou art become the people of the Lord thy God.
27.10: Thou shalt hearken therefore unto the voyce of the Lord thy God, and do his commandements and his ordinances, which I command thee this day.
27.11: And Moses charged the people the same day, saying,
27.12: These shall stand upon mount Gerizzim, to bless the people when ye shall pass over Iorden: Simeon, and Levi, and Judah, and Issachar, and Joseph, and Beniamin.
27.13: And these shall stand upon mount Ebal to curse: Reuben, Gad, and Asher, and Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali.
27.14: And the Levites shall answer and say unto all the men of Israel with a loud voyce,
27.15: Cursed be the man that shall make any carved or molten image, which is an abomination unto the Lord, the work of the hands of the craftesman, and putteth it in a secret place: And all the people shall answer, and say: So be it.
27.16: Cursed be he that curseth his father and his mother: And all the people shall say: So be it.
27.17: Cursed be he that removeth his neighbors mark: And all the people shall say: So be it.
27.18: Cursed be he that maketh ye blind go out of the way: And all the people shall say: So be it.
27.19: Cursed be he that hindreth the right of the stranger, the fatherles, and the widow: And all the people shall say: So be it.
27.20: Cursed be hee that lyeth with his fathers wife: for he hath vncouered his fathers skirt: And all the people shall say: So be it.
27.21: Cursed be he that lieth with any beast: And all the people shall say: So be it.
27.22: Cursed be he that lyeth with his sister, the daughter of his father, or the daughter of his mother: And all the people shall say: So be it.
27.23: Cursed be he that lyeth with his mother in law: And all the people shall say: So be it.
27.24: Cursed be hee that smiteth his neyghbour secretly: And all the people shall say: So be it.
27.25: Cursed be he that taketh a reward to put to death innocent blood: And all the people shall say: So be it.
27.26: Cursed be he that confirmeth not all the wordes of this Law, to do them: And all the people shall say: So be it.

28.1: If thou shalt obey diligently the voyce of the Lord thy God, and observe and do all his commandements, which I command thee this day, then the Lord thy God wil set thee on high above all the nations of the earth.
28.2: And all these blessings shall come on thee, and overtake thee, if thou shalt obey the voyce of the Lord thy God.
28.3: Blessed shalt thou be in the citie, and blessed also in the field.
28.4: Blessed shalbe the fruit of thy body, and ye fruit of thy ground, and the fruit of thy cattel, the increase of thy kine, and ye flocks of thy sheep.
28.5: Blessed shalbe thy basket and thy dough.
28.6: Blessed shalt thou be, whe thou comest in, and blessed also when thou goest out.
28.7: The Lord shall cause thine enemies that rise against thee, to fall before thy face: they shall come out against thee one way, and shall flee before thee leuen wayes.
28.8: The Lord shall command the blessing to be with thee in thy store houses, and in all that thou settest thine hand to, and wil bless thee in the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee.
28.9: The Lord shall make thee an holy people unto himself, as he hath sworn unto thee, if thou shalt keep the commandements of the Lord thy God, and walk in his wayes.
28.10: Then all people of the earth shall see that the Name of the Lord is called upon over thee, and they shalbe afrayde of thee.
28.11: And the Lord shall make thee plenteous in goods, in the fruit of thy body, and in the fruit of thy cattell, and in the fruit of thy ground, in the land which the Lord sware unto thy fathers, to give thee.
28.12: The Lord shall open unto thee his good treasure, even the heaven to give rayne unto thy kind in due season, and to bless all the work of thine handes: and thou shalt lend unto many nations, but shalt not borow thy self.
28.13: And the Lord shall make thee the head, and not the tayle, and thou shalt be above onely, and shalt not bee beneath, if thou obey the commandements of the Lord thy God, which I command thee this day, to keep and to do them.
28.14: But thou shalt not decline from any of the wordes, which I command you this day, either to the right hand or to the left, to goe after other gods to serve them.
28.15: But if thou wilt not obey the voyce of the Lord thy God, to keep and to do all his commandementes and his ordinances, which I command thee this day, then al these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee.
28.16: Cursed shalt thou bee in the town, and cursed also in the field.
28.17: Cursed shall thy basket be, and thy dough.
28.18: Cursed shall be the fruit of thy body, and the fruit of thy land, the increase of thy kine, and the flockes of thy sheep.
28.19: Cursed shalt thou be when thou comest in, and cursed also when thou goest out.
28.20: The Lord shall send upon thee cursing, trouble, and shame, in all that which thou settest thine hand to do, until thou be destroyed, and perish quickely, because of the wickedness of thy workes whereby thou hast forsaken me.
28.21: The Lord shall make the pestilence cleave unto thee, until he hath consumed thee from the land, whither thou goest to possess it.
28.22: The Lord shall smite thee with a consumption, and with the fever, and with a burning ague, and with fervent heat, and with the sword, and with blasting, and with the mildew, and they shall pursue thee until thou perish.
28.23: And thine heaven that is over thine head, shall be brass, and the earth that is under thee, yron.
28.24: The Lord shall give thee for the rayne of thy land, dust and ashes: even from heaven shall it come down upon thee, until thou be destroyed.
28.25: And the Lord shall cause thee to fall before thine enemies: thou shalt come out one way against them, and shalt flee seven wayes before them, and shalt be scattered through all the kingdomes of the earth.
28.26: And thy carkeis shall be meat unto all foules of the ayre, and unto the beasts of the earth, and none shall fray them away.
28.27: The Lord wil smite thee with the botch of Egypt, and with the emeroids, and with the skab, and with the itch, that thou canst not be healed.
28.28: And ye Lord shall smite thee with madnes, and with blindnes, and with astonying of heart.
28.29: Thou shalt also grope at noon daies, as the blind gropeth in darknes, and shalt not prosper in thy wayes: thou shalt never but bee oppressed with wrong and be powled evermore, and no man shall succour thee.
28.30: Thou shalt betroth a wife, and another man shall lye with her: thou shalt build an house, and shalt not dwell therein: thou shalt plant a vineyard, and shalt not eat the fruit.
28.31: Thine oxe shalbe slayne before thine eyes, and thou shalt not eat thereof: thine ass shall be violently taken away before thy face, and shall not be restored to thee: thy sheep shalbe given unto thine enemies, and no man shall rescue them for thee.
28.32: Thy sonnes and thy daughters shalbe given unto another people, and thine eyes shall still look for them, even till they fall out, and there shalbe no power in thine hand.
28.33: The fruit of thy land and all thy labours shall a people, which thou knowest not, eat, and thou shalt never but suffer wrong, and violence alway:
28.34: So that thou shalt be mad for the sight which thine eyes shall see.
28.35: The Lord shall smite thee in the knees, and in the thighes, with a sore botch, that thou canst not be healed: even from the sole of thy foot unto the top of thine head.
28.36: The Lord shall bring thee and thy King (which thou shalt set over thee) unto a nation, which neither thou nor thy fathers have knowen, and there thou shalt serve other gods: even wood and stone,
28.37: And thou shalt be a wonder, a proverb and a common talk among all people, whither the Lord shall carie thee.
28.38: Thou shalt carie out much seed into the field, and shalt gather but litle in: for the grashoppers shall destroy it.
28.39: Thou shalt plant a vineyard, and dress it, but shalt neither drink of the wine, nor gather the grapes: for the wormes shall eat it.
28.40: Thou shalt have Olive trees in all thy coastes, but shalt not anoynt thy self with the oyle: for thine olives shall fall.
28.41: Thou shalt beget sonnes, and daughters, but shalt not have them: for they shall goe into captiuitie.
28.42: All thy trees and fruit of thy land shall the grashopper consume.
28.43: The straunger that is among you, shall clime above thee up on hie, and thou shalt come down beneath alow.
28.44: He shall lend thee, and thou shalt not lend him: he shalbe the head, and thou shalt be ye tayle.
28.45: Moreover, all these curses shall come upon thee, and shall pursue thee and overtake thee, till thou be destroyed, because thou obeyedst not the voyce of the Lord thy God, to keep his commandements, and his ordinances, which he commanded thee:
28.46: And they shalbe upon thee for signes and wonders, and upon thy seed for ever,
28.47: Because thou servedst not the Lord thy God with ioyfulnesse and with a good heart for the abundance of all things.
28.48: Therefore thou shalt serve thine enemies which the Lord shall send upon thee, in hunger and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in need of all things? and he shall put a yoke of yron upon thy neck until he have destroyed thee.
28.49: The Lord shall bring a nation upon thee from far, even from the end of the world, flying swift as an Egle: a nation whose tongue thou shalt not understand:
28.50: A nation of a fierce countenance, which will not regard the person of the old, nor have compassion of the yong.
28.51: The same shall eat the fruit of thy cattell, and the fruit of thy land until thou be destroyed, and he shall leave thee neyther wheat, wine, nor oyle, neither the increase of thy kyne, nor the flockes of thy sheep, until he have brought thee to nought.
28.52: And he shall besiege thee in all thy cities, until thine hie and strong walles fall down, wherein thou trustedst in all the land: and hee shall besiege thee in all thy cities throughout all thy land, which the Lord thy God hath given thee.
28.53: And thou shalt eat the fruit of thy bodie: even the flesh of thy sonnes and thy daughters, which the Lord thy God hath given thee, during the siege and straitness wherein thine enemie shall inclose thee:
28.54: So that the man (that is tender and exceeding deintie among you) shalbe grieved at his brother, and at his wife, that lieth in his bosom, and at the remnant of his children, which hee hath yet left,
28.55: For fear of giving unto any of them of the flesh of his children, whom he shall eat, because he hath nothing left him in that siege, and straitness, wherewith thine enemie shall besiege thee in all thy cities.
28.56: The tender and deintie woman among you, which never would venture to set the sole of her foot upon the ground (for her softnesse and tenderness) shalbe grieved at her husband that lieth in her bosom, and at her sonne, and at her daughter,
28.57: And at her afterbirth (that shall come out from between her feet) and at her childre, which she shall bear: for when all things lack, she shall eat them secretly, during the siege and straitness, wherewith thine enemie shall besiege thee in thy cities.
28.58: If thou wilt not keep and doe all the wordes of the Law (that are written in this book) and fear this glorious and feareful name The Lord Thy God,
28.59: The the Lord wil make thy plagues wonderful, and the plagues of thy seed, even great plagues and of long continuance, and sore diseases, and of long durance.
28.60: Moreover, he will bring upon thee all the diseases of Egypt, whereof thou wast afraid, and they shall cleave unto thee.
28.61: And every sickenesse, and every plague, which is not written in the book of this Law, will the Lord heap upon thee, until thou be destroyed.
28.62: And ye shall be left few in nomber, where ye were as the starres of heaven in multitude, because thou wouldest not obey the voyce of the Lord thy God.
28.63: And as the Lord hath reioyced over you, to doe you good, and to multiply you, so he will reioyce over you, to destroy you, and bring you to nought, and ye shalbe rooted out of the land, whither thou goest to possess it.
28.64: And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the world unto the other, and there thou shalt serve other gods, which thou hast not knowen nor thy fathers, even wood and stone.
28.65: Also among these nations thou shalt find no rest, neither shall the sole of thy foot have rest: for the Lord shall give thee there a trembling heart, and looking to return till thine eyes fall out, and a sorowfull mind.
28.66: And thy life shall hang before thee, and thou shalt fear both night and day, and shalt have none assurance of thy life.
28.67: In the morning thou shalt say, Would God it were evening, and at the evening thou shalt say, Would God it were morning, for ye fear of thine heart, which thou shalt fear, and for the sight of thine eyes, which thou shalt see.
28.68: And the Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with shippes by the way, whereof I said unto thee, Thou shalt see it no more again: and there yee shall sell your selves unto your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen, and there shalbe no byer.

29.1: These are the wordes of the covenant which the Lord commanded Moses to make with the children of Israel in the land of Moab beside the covenant which hee had made with them in Horeb.
29.2: And Moses called all Israel, and said unto them, Ye have seen all that the Lord did before your eyes in the land of Egypt unto Pharaoh and unto all his seruantes, and unto all his land,
29.3: The great tentations which thine eyes have seen, those great miracles and wonders:
29.4: Yet the Lord hath not given you an heart to perceive, and eyes to see, and eares to hear, unto this day.
29.5: And I have led you fourty yere in the wilderness: your clothes are not waxed old upon you, neyther is thy shooe waxed old upon thy foot.
29.6: Ye have eaten no bread, neither drunk wine, nor strong drink, that ye might know how that I am the Lord your God.
29.7: After, ye came unto this place, and Sihon King of Heshbon, and Og King of Bashan came out against us unto battell, and we slew them,
29.8: And took their land, and gave it for an inheritance unto the Reubenites, and to the Gadites, and to the half tribe of Manasseh.
29.9: Keep therefore the wordes of this covenant and doe them, that ye may prosper in all that ye shall doe.
29.10: Ye stand this day every one of you before the Lord your God: your heads of your tribes, your Elders and your officers, eve al ye me of Israel:
29.11: Your children, your wives, and thy stranger that is in thy camp from the hewer of thy wood, unto the drawer of thy water,
29.12: That thou shouldest pass into the covenant of the Lord thy God, and into his othe which the Lord thy God maketh with thee this day,
29.13: For to establish thee this day a people unto him self, and that he may be unto thee a God, as he hath said unto thee, and as he hath sworn unto thy fathers, Abraham, Izhak, and Iaakob.
29.14: Neither make I this covenant, and this othe with you onely,
29.15: But aswel with him that standeth here with us this day before the Lord our God, as with him that is not here with us this day.
29.16: For ye know, how we have dwelt in the land of Egypt, and how we passed thorowe the middes of the nations, which ye passed by.
29.17: And ye have seen their abominations and their idoles (wood, and stone, silver and gold) which were among them,
29.18: That there should not be among you man nor woman, nor familie, nor tribe, which should turn his heart away this day from the Lord our God, to goe and serve the gods of these nations, and that there should not be among you any root that bringeth forth gall and wormewood,
29.19: So that when he heareth the words of this curse, he bless him self in his heart, saying, I shall have peace, although I walk according to the stubburnes of mine own heart, thus adding drunkenness to thirst.
29.20: The Lord will not be merciful unto him, but then the wrath of the Lord and his ielousie shall smoke against that man, and every curse that is written in this book, shall light upon him, and the Lord shall put out his name from under heaven,
29.21: And the Lord shall separate him unto evil out of all the tribes of Israel, according unto all the curses of the covenant, that is written in the book of this Law.
29.22: So that the generatio to come, even your children, that shall rise up after you, and the stranger, that shall come from a far land, shall say, when they shall see the plagues of this land, and the diseases thereof, wherewith the Lord shall smite it:
29.23: (For all that land shall burn with brimstone and salt: it shall not be sowen, nor bring forth, nor any grass shall grow therein, like as in the ouerthrowing of Sodom, and Gomorah, Admah, and Zeboim, which the Lord overthrew in his wrath and in his anger)
29.24: Then shall all nations say, Wherefore hath the Lord done thus unto this land? how fierce is this great wrath?
29.25: And they shall answer, Because they have forsaken the covenant of the Lord God of their fathers, which he had made with them, when he brought them out of the land of Egypt,
29.26: And went and served other gods and worshipped them: even gods which they knew not, and which had given them nothing,
29.27: Therefore the wrath of the Lord waxed hot against this land, to bring upon it every curse that is written in this book.
29.28: And ye Lord hath rooted them out of their land in anger, and in wrath, and in great indignation, and hath cast them into another land, as appeareth this day.
29.29: The secret things belong to the Lord our God, but the things reueiled belong unto us, and to our children for ever, that we may doe all the wordes of this Law.

30.1: Now when all these things shall come upon thee, either the blessing or the curse which I have set before thee, and thou shalt turn into thine heart, among all the nations whither the Lord thy God hath driven thee,
30.2: And shalt return unto the Lord thy God, and obey his voyce in all that I commaund thee this day: thou, and thy children with all thine heart and with all thy soul,
30.3: Then the Lord thy God wil cause thy captives to return, and have compassion upon thee, and wil return, to gather thee out of all the people, where the Lord thy God had scattered thee.
30.4: Though thou werest cast unto the utmost part of heaven, from thence will the Lord thy God gather thee, and from thence wil he take thee,
30.5: And the Lord thy God will bring thee into the land which thy fathers possessed, and thou shalt possess it, and he will shew thee fauour, and will multiplie thee above thy fathers.
30.6: And the Lord thy God will circumcise thine heart, and the heart of thy seed, that thou mayest love the Lord thy God with all thine heart, and with al thy soul, that thou maiest live.
30.7: And the Lord thy God will lay all these curses upon thine enemies, and on them, that hate thee, and that persecute thee.
30.8: Return thou therefore, and obey the voyce of the Lord, and do all his commandements, which I commaund thee this day.
30.9: And the Lord thy God will make thee plenteous in every work of thine hand, in the fruit of thy bodie, and in the fruit of thy cattel, and in the fruit of the land for thy wealth: for the Lord will turn again, and reioyce over thee to do thee good, as he reioyced over thy fathers,
30.10: Because thou shalt obey the voyce of the Lord thy God, in keeping his comandements, and his ordinances, which are written in the book of this Law, when thou shalt return unto the Lord thy God with all thine heart and with al thy soul.
30.11: For this commandement which I command thee this day, is not hid from thee, neither is it far off.
30.12: It is not in heaven, that thou shouldest say, Who shall go up for us to heaven, and bring it us, and cause us to hear it, that we may doe it?
30.13: Neither is it beyond the sea, that thou shouldest say, Who shall go over the sea for us, and bring it us, and cause us to hear it, that we may do it?
30.14: But the word is very neere unto thee: even in thy mouth and in thine heart, for to do it.
30.15: Behold, I have set before thee this day life and good, death and evil,
30.16: In that I commaund thee this day, to love the Lord thy God, to walk in his wayes, and to keep his commandements, and his ordinances, and his lawes, that thou mayest live, and be multiplied, and that the Lord thy God may bless thee in the land, whither thou goest to possess it.
30.17: But if thine heart turn away, so that thou wilt not obey, but shalt be seduced and worship other gods, and serve them,
30.18: I pronounce unto you this day, that ye shall surely perish, ye shall not prolong your dayes in the land, whither thou passest over Iorden to possess it.
30.19: I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing. therefore chuse life, that both thou and thy seed may live,
30.20: By loving the Lord thy God, by obeying his voyce, and by cleauing unto him: for he is thy life, and the length of thy dayes: that thou mayest dwell in the land which the Lord sware unto thy fathers, Abraham, Izhak, and Iaakob, to give them.

31.1: Then Moses went and spake these wordes unto all Israel,
31.2: And said unto them, I am an hundreth and twentie yeere old this day: I can no more goe out and in: also the Lord hath said unto me, Thou shalt not goe over this Iorden.
31.3: The Lord thy God he will go over before thee: he will destroy these nations before thee, and thou shalt possess them. Joshua, he shall goe before thee, as the Lord hath said.
31.4: And the Lord shall doe unto them, as he did to Sihon and to Og Kings of the Amorites: and unto their land whom he destroyed.
31.5: And the Lord shall give them before you that ye may do unto them according unto every commandement, which I have comanded you.
31.6: Pluck up your hearts therefore, and be strong: dread not, nor be afraid of them: for the Lord thy God him self doeth goe with thee: he will not fail thee, nor forsake thee.
31.7: And Moses called Joshua, and said unto him in the sight of all Israel, Be of a good courage and strong: for thou shalt go with this people unto the land which the Lord hath sworn unto their fathers, to give them, and thou shalt give it them to inherit.
31.8: And the Lord him self doeth go before thee: he will be with thee: he will not fail thee, neither forsake thee: fear not therefore, nor be discomforted.
31.9: And Moses wrote this Law, and delivered it unto the Priestes the sonnes of Levi (which bare the Ark of the covenant of the Lord) and unto all the Elders of Israel,
31.10: And Moses commanded them, saying, Every seventh yeere when the yeere of freedom shalbe in the feast of the Tabernacles:
31.11: When all Israel shall come to appear before the Lord thy God, in the place which he shall chuse, thou shalt read this Law before all Israel that they may hear it.
31.12: Gather the people together: men, and women, and children, and thy stranger that is within thy gates, that they may hear, and that they may learn, and fear the Lord your God, and keep and observe all the wordes of this Law,
31.13: And that their children which have not knowen it, may hear it, and learn to fear the Lord your God, as long as ye live in the land, whither ye goe over Iorden to possess it.
31.14: Then the Lord said unto Moses, Behold, thy dayes are come, that thou must die: Call Joshua, and stand ye in the Tabernacle of the Congregation that I may give him a charge. So Moses and Joshua went, and stood in the Tabernacle of the Congregation.
31.15: And the Lord appeared in the Tabernacle, in the pillar of a cloud: and the pillar of the cloud stood over the door of the Tabernacle.
31.16: And the Lord said unto Moses, Behold, thou shalt sleep with thy fathers, and this people will rise up, and goe a whoring after the gods of a strange land (whither they goe to dwell therein) and will forsake me, and break my covenant which I have made with them.
31.17: Wherefore my wrath will wax hot against them at that day, and I will forsake them, and will hide my face from them: then they shalbe consumed, and many adversities and tribulations shall come upon them: so then they will say, Are not these troubles come upon me, because God is not with me?
31.18: But I will surely hide my face in that day, because of all the evil, which they shall commit, in that they are turned unto other gods.
31.19: Now therefore write ye this song for you, and teach it the children of Israel: put it in their mouthes, that this song may be my witness against the children of Israel.
31.20: For I will bring them into the land (which I sware unto their fathers) that floweth with milk and honie, and they shall eat, and fil them selves, and wax fat: then shall they turn unto other gods, and serve them, and contemn me, and break my covenant.
31.21: And then when many adversities and tribulations shall come upon them, this song shall answer them to their face as a witness: for it shall not be forgotte out of the mouthes of their posteritie: for I know their imagination, which they goe about even now, before I have brought them into the land which I sware.
31.22: Moses therefore wrote this song the same day and taught it the children of Israel.
31.23: And God gave Joshua the sonne of Nun a charge, and said, Be strong, and of a good courage: for thou shalt bring the children of Israel into the land, which I sware unto them, and I will be with thee.
31.24: And when Moses had made an end of writing the wordes of this Law in a book until he had finished them,
31.25: Then Moses commanded the Levites, which bare the Ark of the covenant of the Lord, saying,
31.26: Take the book of this Law, and put ye it in the side of the Ark of the covenant of the Lord your God, that it may be there for a witnes against thee.
31.27: For I know thy rebellion and thy stiff neck: behold, I being yet alive with you this day, ye are rebellious against the Lord: how much more then after my death?
31.28: Gather unto me all the Elders of your tribes, and your officers, that I may speak these wordes in their audience, and call heaven and earth to record against them.
31.29: For I am sure that after my death ye will utterly be corrupt and turn from the way, which I have commanded you: therefore evil will come upon you at the length, because ye will comit evil in the sight of the Lord, by provoking him to anger through the work of your hands.
31.30: Thus Moses spake in the audience of all the congregation of Israel the wordes of this song, until he had ended them.

32.1: Hearken, ye heavens, and I will speak: and let the earth hear the words of my mouth.
32.2: My doctrine shall drop as the rain, and my speach shall stil as the dew, as the showre upon the herbes, and as the great rain upon the grass.
32.3: For I will publish the name of the Lord: give ye glorie unto our God.
32.4: Perfect is the work of the mighty God: for all his wayes are iudgement. God is true, and without wickedness: just, and righteous is he.
32.5: They have corrupted them selves toward him by their vice, not being his children, but a froward and crooked generation.
32.6: Doe ye so reward the Lord, O foolish people and unwise? is not he thy father, that hath bought thee? he hath made thee, and proportioned thee.
32.7: Remember the dayes of old: consider the yeeres of so many generations: ask thy father, and he will shew thee: thine Elders, and they will tell thee.
32.8: When the most hie God deuided to the nations their inheritance, when he separated the sonnes of Adam, he appoynted the borders of the people, according to the nomber of the children of Israel.
32.9: For the Lordes portion is his people: Iaakob is the lot of his inheritance.
32.10: He found him in ye land of ye wildernes, in a waste, and roaring wildernes: he led him about, he taught him, and kept him as ye apple of his eye.
32.11: As an eagle stereth up her nest, flootereth over her birdes, stretcheth out her wings, taketh them, and beareth them on her wings,
32.12: So the Lord alone led him, and there was no strange god with him.
32.13: He caryed him up to the hie places of the earth, that he might eat the fruites of the fieldes, and he caused him to suck hony out of the stone, and oyle out of the hard rock:
32.14: Butter of kine, and milk of sheep with fat of the lambes, and rammes fed in Bashan, and goates, with the fat of the graines of wheat, and the red licour of the grape hast thou drunk.
32.15: But he that should have been upright, when he waxed fat, spurned with his heel: thou art fat, thou art gross, thou art laden with fatnes: therefore he forsook God that made him, and regarded not the strong God of his salvation.
32.16: They provoked him with strange gods: they provoked him to anger with abominations.
32.17: They offred unto devils, not to God, but to gods whom they knew not: new gods that came newly up, whom their fathers feared not.
32.18: Thou hast forgotten the mightie God that begat thee, and hast forgotten God that formed thee.
32.19: The Lord then saw it, and was angrie, for the provocation of his sonnes and of his daughters.
32.20: And he said, I will hide my face from the: I will see what their end shalbe: for they are a froward generation, children in who is no faith.
32.21: They have moved me to ielousie with that which is not God: they have provoked me to anger with their vanities: and I will move them to ielousie with those which are no people: I wil provoke them to anger with a foolish nation.
32.22: For fire is kindled in my wrath, and shall burn unto the bottom of hell, and shall consume the earth with her increase, and set on fire the foundations of the mountaines.
32.23: I will spend plagues upon them: I will bestow mine arrowes upon them.
32.24: They shalbe burnt with hunger, and consumed with heat, and with bitter destruction: I will also send the teeth of beastes upon them, with the venime of serpents creeping in the dust.
32.25: The sword shall kill them without, and in the chambers fear: both the yong man and the yong woman, the suckeling with the man of gray hear.
32.26: I have said, I would scatter them abroad: I would make their remembrance to cease from among men,
32.27: Save that I feared the furie of the enemie, least their adversaries should wax proud, and least they should say, Our hie hand and not the Lord hath done all this:
32.28: For they are a nation void of counsel, neither is there any understanding in them.
32.29: Oh that they were wise, then they would understand this: they would consider their latter end.
32.30: How should one chase a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight, except their strong God had sold the, and the Lord had shut them up?
32.31: For their god is not as our God, even our enemies being judges.
32.32: For their vine is of the vine of Sodom, and of the vines of Gomorah: their grapes are grapes of gall, their clusters be bitter.
32.33: Their wine is the poyson of dragons, and the cruel gall of aspes.
32.34: Is not this laid in store with me, and sealed up among my treasures?
32.35: Vengeance and recompence are mine: their foot shall slide in due time: for the day of their destruction is at hand, and the things that shall come upon them, make haste.
32.36: For the Lord shall judge his people, and repent toward his servants, when hee seeth that their power is gone, and none shut up in hold nor left abroad.
32.37: When men shall say, Where are their gods, their mighty God in whom they trusted,
32.38: Which did eat the fat of their sacrifices, and did drink the wine of their drink offring? let them rise up, and help you: let him be your refuge.
32.39: Behold now, for I, I am he, and there is no gods with me: I kill, and give life: I wound, and I make whole: neither is there any that can deliver out of mine hand.
32.40: For I lift up mine hand to heaven, and say, I live for ever.
32.41: If I whet my glittering sword, and mine hand take hold on iudgement, I will execute vengeance on mine enemies, and will reward them that hate me.
32.42: I will make mine arrowes drunk with blood, (and my sword shall eat flesh) for the blood of the slain, and of the captives, when I beginne to take vengeance of the enemie.
32.43: Ye nations, praise his people: for he will avenge the blood of his servants, and will execute vengeance upon his adversaries, and will bee merciful unto his land, and to his people.
32.44: Then Moses came and spake all ye words of this song in the audience of the people, he and Hoshea the sonne of Nun.
32.45: When Moses had made an end of speaking all these wordes to all Israel,
32.46: Then hee said unto them, Set your heartes unto all the wordes which I testifie against you this day, that ye may command them unto your children, that they may observe and doo all the wordes of this Law.
32.47: For it is no vain word concerning you, but it is your life, and by this word ye shall prolong your dayes in the land, whither yee go over Iorden to possess it.
32.48: And the Lord spake unto Moses the self same day, saying,
32.49: Goe up into the mountain of Abarim, unto the mount Nebo, which is in the land of Moab, that is over against Jericho: and behold the land of Canaan, which I give unto the children of Israel for a possession,
32.50: And die in the mount which thou goest up unto, and thou shalt be gathered unto thy people, as Aaron thy brother died in mount Hor, and was gathered unto his people,
32.51: Because ye trespassed against me among the children of Israel, at the waters of Meribah, at Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin: for ye sanctified me not among the children of Israel.
32.52: Thou shalt therefore see the land before thee, but shalt not go thither, I mean, into the land which I give the children of Israel.

33.1: Now this is the blessing wherewith Moses the man of God blessed the children of Israel before his death, and said,
33.2: The Lord came from Sinai, and rose up from Seir unto them, and appeared clearely from mount Paran, and he came with ten thousands of Saints, and at his right hand a firie Law for them.
33.3: Though hee love the people, yet all thy Saints are in thine handes: and they are humbled at thy foete, to receive thy words.
33.4: Moses commanded us a Law for an inheritance of the Congregation of Iaakob.
33.5: Then he was among the righteous people, as King, when the heades of the people, and the tribes of Israel were assembled.
33.6: Let Reuben live, and not die, though his men be a small nomber.
